messages:
mike: quick thought — our current quota attribution is weird when proxying requests from internal services. thinking about adding an X-Origin-Project header so the billing/telemetry stack attributes tokens to the originating project rather than the proxying service.
jen: can you sketch the exact use-case? is this mostly for cross-project delegations or for agent-like proxies that fan out?
omar: both. e.g., analytics pipeline (shared worker) submits on behalf of many projects. right now quota shows on the worker's service key, not the tenant.
elaine: +1 for better attribution, but worried about spoofing. how will we authenticate origin_project?
mike: plan is that only trusted proxies can pass the header and the edge auth layer will verify the proxy token includes claim: can_forward_origin=true and a whitelist. otherwise header ignored.
ryan: pseudo-API model:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer proxy-token
  X-Origin-Project: proj:acme:42
```
edge will intercept and map attribution if proxy-token has allowance for proj:acme:42.
jen: need to record both "effective_actor" (worker) and "billed_project" (acme) in telemetry. dashboards should show both.
omar: telemetry events: attributed_tokens, original_project_id, proxy_service_id, verification_status. that should let us debug misattribution.
elaine: ok but what about quota enforcement? if acme is out of quota, should proxy be blocked or should it fall back to a paid path?
mike: proposal: default = enforce billed_project quota. fallback policy config on proxy can opt into using proxy's pool if billed_project denies, but that requires explicit consent and double-billing safeguards.
ryan: console UX: we need a clear row in usage table for "attributed via proxy" with link to proxy service. Also a filter to show only origin projects.
jen: rollout caveats: we'll add a feature-flag on edge. step 1: telemetry-only mode (record attribution but don't change billing). step 2: canary billing for trusted customers. step 3: enforce globally.
omar: agree. also add sampling for legacy proxies to avoid noisy metrics.
elaine: security checklist: 1) token claim validation 2) audit log entry for attr change 3) denylist for header on public endpoints 4) integration test asserting spoofing rejected.
ryan: metrics to add to Redwood Console: quota_mismatch_rate, attribution_verification_failures, tokens_attributed_per_proxy. these should be in per-route dashboards.
mike: internal API change: auth service will expose /v1/validate-origin?proxy_token=&origin_project= which edge can call (cacheable). cheap call + TTL.
jen: can we make that an introspect cache in edge to avoid spikes? TTL and a local LRU should be fine.
omar: also add a small event to the event bus when attribution happens so billing pipeline can backfill in case of late processing.
deploy-bot: deploy-started edge/auth:v2 with feature-flag origin-attribution=false
mike: next steps: write RFC w/ schema for X-Origin-Project, auth claim name (forward_allowed_projects), console wireframes for attribution column, and a phased rollout checklist. assigning owners: RFC (mike), telemetry schema (omar), console mocks (ryan), security review (elaine).
jen: ping me once RFC is up, I'll coordinate canary customers list. :+1:
ryan: will sketch dashboard mockups today, dropping links in the RFC.
mike: cool — thanks all. I'll create the RFC and tag owners.
